summary: Full regression of iteration-review items on web (backend + web UI). 36/36 backend pytest cases pass (1 skipped: no prescreen items seeded). Found and fixed one CRITICAL frontend compile bug (React hooks violation in AdminPage.jsx) that was blocking the entire SPA — webpack-dev-server overlay was intercepting every click because useState was called conditionally after early returns. After fix, all web flows (admin login→/admin with Workspace btn, UW/Partner login→/workspace, client login→/dashboard, Book Discovery hidden when logged in, Admin Console tabs render, Manage access modal opens with partner+UW roles) pass end-to-end. All 11 review items verified: AI RBAC, 200MB cap (and 413 on >200MB), underwriter admin-parity visibility, partner internal perms + settings/users 403, inbox scope=all for admin+UW, prescreen status=missing accepted, inline preview Content-Disposition=inline, deal messages access for admin/UW/partner, PUT /api/admin/users/{clientId}/access assigns valid partner ids and filters bogus ones (partner gains deal access after assign), PATCH /workspace/transactions accepts engagement/diligence/close dates, Admin Console tabs render.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED by testing agent — Rule-of-Hooks violation: useState for accessClient/accessIds were declared on lines 79-80 after three early return guards (lines 44-46), causing a compile error 'React Hook useState is called conditionally'. The webpack-dev-server error overlay (iframe#webpack-dev-server-client-overlay) was intercepting pointer events on EVERY page across the SPA, which would have blocked every button in production as well (dev-only overlay would simply hide the UI). Hoisted the two useState calls to the top of the component next to the other hooks. Reference: /app/frontend/src/pages/AdminPage.jsx:16-24. VERIFIED: frontend recompiles cleanly, SPA fully usable, all 4 role flows pass.

action_items: Review the AdminPage.jsx hoisting (/app/frontend/src/pages/AdminPage.jsx:16-24). The two moved hooks are purely state — behaviourally identical, but the main agent should spot-check in case there is a hidden intent to late-declare them.

Transient 503 observed once from Emergent object storage (/api/uploads/{id}/download) during the inline-preview test on first run; immediate retry succeeded. Not a product bug but worth noting if the service continues to flake.

Prescreen status-dropdown PUT test is skipped unless at least one prescreen has items; main agent can either seed a prescreen or ignore (endpoint shape verified separately via Model schema accepts 'missing').
critical_code_review_comments: AdminPage.jsx:16-24 (fixed) — Hooks were called after early returns, which React detects and treats as a parse-time error in strict ESLint mode. This is a trap when adding a modal to a page that already has guard clauses; always declare state at the top.

server.py:1708 admin_set_client_access — correctly validates assigned_ids against account_type∈{partner,underwriter} and strips invalid ids. Good. However, there is no auditing: a silent downgrade (bogus id dropped) returns 200 with filtered list — consider surfacing in response if ids were rejected.
server.py:1392 inbox scope=all — only honoured for admin or underwriter; falls back to own for other inbox users. Clean.
workspace/core.py PERMS — PARTNER has {'read','write','message','internal'} but NOT 'manage'/'delete'/'review'/'ai'. Correct per the spec.

crm_routes.py update_transaction — accepts engagement_date/diligence_date/close_date via Pydantic regex. The validate_dates helper enforces order only if close_date is in the patch, which may let an inconsistent partial update slip through if only engagement_date is PATCHed to a date after an existing close_date. Minor edge case.

rca of the issue: AdminPage.jsx bug RCA — The Manage Access modal was added recently and placed state hooks inline next to the helper function at line 79, right below three early-return guards for user auth state (user===null, user===false, user.role!==admin). The React hooks runtime detects conditional invocation at the second render (when the guard returns before the hooks run) and the CRA build pipeline promotes react-hooks/rules-of-hooks to an eslint ERROR, which triggers the webpack dev-server error overlay. The overlay is a full-page <iframe id='webpack-dev-server-client-overlay'> inserted on top of the DOM, intercepting pointer events across the whole SPA — hence every click (login, nav, tab) was dead on arrival. Fix: hoist useState(accessClient) and useState(accessIds) to the state block at the top of the component (lines 18-24). Verified by re-running the full role matrix after the fix — all four roles log in and reach the expected landing page.
